result: The authors identified a T7 RNAP promoter variant (T7 T10 GG or T7 G10 GG) that ensures high editing rates across Leishmania species without compromising parasite growth. Using a dual-construct system, complete knockdown of the tdTomato reporter was achieved with all T7 RNAP promoter variants, while the unmodified T7 promoter caused an almost twofold increase in doubling time. The modified promoters (T7 T10 GG, T7 G10 GG) resulted in no significant growth rate increase, with doubling times ranging from 7.5 to 8.1 hr, and complete tdTomato depletion was achieved in just 7 days compared to 33 days previously.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirm this finding, with one stating 'Fig.1 clearly describes reduced impairment in growth of parasites expressing sgRNAs via changes in promoters' and another noting the authors 'significantly reduce the non-specific toxicity of sgRNA expression whilst retaining high editing efficiencies.' The editor describes this as part of a 'meticulously-developed improved strategy' with 'reduced background toxicity.'

result: The authors created a triple-expression construct for stable integration of CBE sgRNA expression cassettes into the 18S rRNA SSU locus using AsCas12a ultra-mediated DNA double-strand breaks. This approach increased transfection efficiency by ~400-fold to 1 transfectant per 70 transfected cells. Cas12a-induced DSBs increased the rate of correct donor DNA integration irrespective of homology flank length, with Cas12a crRNA-4 performing significantly better than other crRNAs. High transfection efficiencies were reached, yielding up to one transfectant out of ~470 transfected parasites, with the Lonza Nucleofector technology boosting efficiency by an additional 20-fold.
evaluation: Reviewers strongly support this finding, with one noting 'Figs.2 and 3 compellingly document the usefulness of using AsCas12a for integration after transformation' and another stating the authors 'increase the transfection efficiency 400-fold.' A reviewer explicitly confirms 'The cell editing frequency of 1 edit per 70 cells reported in this study represents a 400-fold improvement over the previously published protocol.'

result: Using the improved system, complete depletion of the tdTomato signal was observed just 7 days post transfection in all tested species when integrating CBE sgRNA expression cassettes into the 18S rRNA SSU locus. The expression of CBE, T7 RNAP, AsCas12a ultra, and the CBE sgRNA had minimal or no impact on parasite growth across all three species. In L. major, the homo-polymer was fully introduced in 14 days using the T7 RNAP promoter-based dual vector system, while no editing was observed with the ribosomal promoter system. Just 6 days post transfection, the PF16 target site was fully edited and the overwhelming majority of cells were paralyzed. Illumina and ONT sequencing confirmed that cassettes integrated on separate alleles with only one CBE sgRNA cassette copy per L. mexicana cell.
evaluation: Reviewers affirm these findings, with one stating 'Figs.1 and 4 demonstrate the capacity of the combined modifications to efficiently edit a gene in three different Leishmania species.' The editor describes the work as 'meticulously-developed' with 'enhanced efficiency relative to a previously-described method.' No concerns are raised about the editing efficiency or integration data.

result: Using the improved system for a small-scale proof-of-principle pooled screen, the authors successfully confirmed the essential and fitness-associated functions of CK1.2, CRK2, CRK3, AUK1/AIRK, TOR1, IFT88, IFT139, IFT140, and RAB5A in Leishmania mexicana. sgRNAs targeting essential and fitness-associated genes were strongly depleted, while non-targeting control sgRNAs remained unchanged. Only two IFT88, two CRK3, and one CRK2 sgRNAs showed no reduction in abundance. The comparison between method v1 and v2 revealed significant improvements, with the new method achieving ~10–20× stronger ratios with substantially reduced error margins for the non-targeting controls.
evaluation: Reviewers strongly support this finding, with one stating 'Fig. 5 shows that this approach can be conducted at scale, providing a means of assessing the fitness of mutant pools.' The editor notes the authors 'show use of the strategy in a small-scale loss-of-function screen, providing compelling evidence that large-scale screens will be possible.' A reviewer confirms the authors 'validate this tool in a small-scale loss of function screen incorporating essential and non-essential genes, identifying the expected growth phenotypes.'

result: The authors demonstrate the utility of co-expressing AsCas12a ultra, T7 RNAP, and CBE for hybrid CRISPR gene replacement and base editing within the same cell line. They show that the introduction of a thymidine homo-polymer within the PF16 CDS produces the same motility phenotype observed when using gene replacement strategies for knockout generation. The ORF was successfully replaced by drug-resistance markers on both alleles, confirmed by Sanger sequencing, and motility analysis revealed the expected PF16 motility phenotype.
evaluation: Reviewers affirm this finding, with one noting 'Figs.1 and 4 demonstrate the capacity of the combined modifications to efficiently edit a gene in three different Leishmania species.' The editor describes the work as 'meticulously-developed' and reviewers raise no concerns about the hybrid approach or the validation experiments.

result: The authors developed a revised CBE sgRNA scoring system to prioritize STOP codon generation. A C-score was implemented that determines the ratio of available cytosines to resulting STOP codons. The new scoring system rates CBE sgRNAs higher when the STOP codon is introduced within positions 4–8 and lower when introduced within positions 11–12.
evaluation: Reviewers implicitly accept this improvement as part of the overall methodological advances. One reviewer notes the authors 'improve the sgRNA design' and predicts 'null mutants will be more efficiently produced after editing.' No concerns are raised about the scoring system.

result: All tested L. mexicana clones showed only unique sequencing reads, confirming the integration of only one guide per transfectant. However, for L. donovani and L. major, 2 out of 10 sequencing reads showed mixed guide sequences, suggesting that multiple CBE sgRNAs can be integrated per cell. The integration of multiple sgRNAs per cell remained random in L. donovani and L. major.
evaluation: Reviewers accept this finding as part of the overall characterization of the system. One reviewer notes the authors 'ensure that only a single sgRNA expression cassette integrates that edits with high efficiencies,' acknowledging the species-specific differences. No concerns are raised about the mixed integration in some species.

result: The authors conclude that these improvements will broaden the range of possible gene editing applications in Leishmania species and will enable a variety of loss-of-function screens in the near future. The improved toolbox sets the stage for various gene editing applications in Leishmania, including genome-wide CBE screens.
evaluation: Reviewers strongly support this conclusion. The editor states the work provides 'compelling evidence that large-scale screens will be possible' and that 'The newly developed tools will be of great interest to researchers working with Leishmania and beyond.' A reviewer confirms 'The combination of these two improvements should open the door to exciting large-scale screens' and 'we have no doubt that the technology established here, will be very useful for the Leishmania research community and beyond.'
